findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment: There were four packages of turkey and Colby jack protein packs that were observed to be above 41F in the open-air cooler. These packages probed at the following temperatures: 51F, 48F, 47F, and 46F. Discussed making sure not to have TCS food items in the corners of the open-air cooler, where they are out of the range of proper cold holding. Ensure that TCS foods are held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There are water bottles observed to be stored outside in front of the facility. Water bottles should not be stored outside, as they are not in a safe, protected location. Ensure that water bottles are stored inside to protect them from contamination from the sun and other miscellaneous sources.
findings.citation_text: 3-307.11 Miscellaneous Sources of Contamination. FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301 - 3-306.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.comment:
There are boxes of single-service articles that are observed to be stored on the floor. Ensure that single-service articles and utensils are stored at least six inches off of the ground. 

There are also pans that are stored with the food-contact surface exposed to contamination on the top clean dish shelf. Ensure that these pans are inverted to protect them from contamination. 

Ensure that single-service articles and utensils are stored inverted or under a covered shelf and are stored at least SIX inches off of the ground.
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food handler training
findings.comment:
The facility uses ShiftSmart to do their food preparation for them. The ShiftSmart employee was present and cooking food during today’s inspection. The employee did not have a food handler card. The employee showed the inspector their phone and the app that they use stated that “A food handler card is not needed to do food preparation in this area”. A food handler card is needed for every food employee that works in a facility that handles food or ice. Ensure that all employees doing food preparation in the facility have a food handler card. 

410 ILCS 625/3.06(b). Food handler training: restaurants. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all food handlers employed by a restaurant, other than someone holding a food service sanitation manager certificate, must receive or obtain American National Standards Institute-accredited training in basic safe food handling principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 3.05 of this Act, food handlers employed in nursing homes, licensed day care homes and facilities, hospitals, schools, and long-term care facilities must renew their training every 3 years. There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training. The training indicated in subsections (e) and (f) of this Section is transferable between employers, but not individuals. The training indicated in subsections (c) and (d) of this Section is not transferable between individuals or employers. Proof that a food handler has been trained must be available upon reasonable request by a State or local health department inspector and may be provided electronically.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: The Quaternary ammonium sanitizer bucket was observed to only be at a concentration of 100ppm. The recommended concentration for Quat is 200 to 400ppm. CORRECTED- The sanitizer bucket was remade and tested to be at a concentration of 200ppm. Ensure that all sanitizer buckets are routinely tested and changed if not at the recommended concentration on the label. 

Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less.

Staff was educated on this during the inspection. 

 (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17  (P) Observed no date mark on french vanilla creamer bag. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Reference 3-501.17.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Observed use by date to be 09/08 on bag of whipped topping.  Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge.  Reference 3-501.17.
